plans.note: Separate caps for each side in 9.1 (IBM) and 9.2 (Customer); check cap amount/formula, mutuality, and exclusion of consequential damages, plus carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality, data breach and fees. 5.4 may add disclaimers of liability and 14.14 shortens the actions period, which functionally limits recovery.

8.1 is IBM's indemnity (test IP infringement scope, defense/settlement control, remedies); 8.2 is our indemnity, which should be narrowed to our content/data and our breach; sec-1 appears to be the indemnity procedure conditions (notice, cooperation) applicable to claims against Customer.

14.16 'Freedom of Action' typically preserves IBM's freedom; confirm it does not reciprocally restrict our business, and check 14.11 (No Resale) and 14.17 (Limitation of Licenses) for de facto restrictions on what we may build, buy or offer.
No exclusivity heading in the outline; most likely nowhere, but verify 14.16/14.11 and the services and charges provisions for sole-source or 'all requirements' language before concluding absent.
No MFN heading; scan 4.1 Charges and 13.3 Amendments for any pricing-parity or best-terms undertaking running against us. Direction check only — an MFN in our favour is acceptable.
14.8 'Personnel' is the likely home for any hiring/solicitation restriction; test whether it binds Customer, its duration, and whether general advertising and unsolicited applicants are carved out.

3.4 governs convenience termination — check whether the right is mutual (we want it one-way in our favour), notice length, and any termination charges or unwind fees, which may cross-reference 3.5 and 4.1.
3.2 Renewal: test for automatic renewal, length of the non-renewal notice window (we want no more than 30 days) and any uncapped price increase on renewal; read with 3.1 Term and 4.1 Charges.

14.3 Choice of Law is the operative clause — confirm it names an accepted jurisdiction and that venue is a court, not foreign arbitration; 14.4 waives jury trial (flag) and 14.19 Geographic Scope may affect applicable law by location.

14.10 Assignment: seek our right to assign to affiliates and to a successor in a merger or asset sale without consent, and delete any IBM right to terminate or consent-gate on our change of control (check 3.3 for a linked termination trigger).

Direction check: 12.1 License and 14.17 Limitation of Licenses define the IP allocation — ensure no grant or assignment of our content, data or marks to IBM beyond what is needed to deliver the services. 11.6 (Content and Digital Certificates), 14.18 (Data Protection) and 14.6 (Publicity and Trademarks) carry Customer Data and mark-use rights.

12.1 is the grant — test scope for affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, whether it is revocable/at-will or suspendable, and territorial limits; 14.17 likely narrows it and 12.2 covers maintenance of Base Components.

No standalone audit clause; 11.3 Suspected Violations is the closest analogue (investigation/access rights against us) and 13.2 AUP may support it. Test for notice, frequency, business-hours limits, confidentiality and who bears cost.

Direction check: look in 4.2 Payment for late-payment interest or penalty charges and in 4.1 for termination/shortfall charges payable by us; confirm no liquidated damages run against Customer. Note whether any service-credit remedy exists in our favour (11.1).

5.1 is IBM's warranty — test duration, workmanlike/conformity standard and the remedy; 5.2 and 5.4 disclaim implied warranties (resist a bare 'AS IS'); 11.1 Services Support and 12.2 Maintenance carry the performance commitments; 11.2 contains our reciprocal warranties.

No insurance heading in the outline; likely absent. Given IBM hosts our data (5.3 Security, 14.18 Data Protection), propose standard coverages (commercial general liability, professional/cyber liability) or accept a self-insurance representation as fallback. 14.12 Risk of Loss is the nearest related clause.

Check 4.1 Charges (and any Order Form/Service Option Attachment cross-reference) for committed volumes, minimum monthly charges or take-or-pay; 11.5 Capacity Planning may impose committed capacity. Ensure any commitment pairs with a convenience exit under 3.4.

3.5 Effect of Termination is the natural home — test for return/export of Customer Data in a usable format, a defined wind-down period and priced transition assistance; 14.2 Survival should carry these obligations, and 14.18/11.6 govern data handling and deletion.
